manifest.description: Measures a GitHub repository before it changes it. Designs a calibrated performance metric (the ruler), proves the metric is trustworthy against a known win, then runs keep-or-revert improvement cycles: every candidate fix is written in an isolated worktree, gated against an edit allowlist and the repo's own tests, and kept only when the measured win clears the noise band. Survivors are drafted as GitHub pull requests you review and publish yourself.
manifest.highlight_1: Proves its own metric first — a run refuses to start on an untrustworthy ruler
manifest.highlight_2: Every candidate is measured A/B, or RED/GREEN for bug fixes, never just 'looks right'
manifest.highlight_3: Keeps a change only when the win clears the measured noise band
manifest.highlight_4: Drafts GitHub pull requests — draft-only, never published or merged for you
manifest.highlight_5: Works on a push-disabled clone, so nothing escapes the sandbox unreviewed
manifest.highlight_6: One resumable chat session per pull request, finding, and run
manifest.use_case_1: Prove measurable performance gains or reproducible bug fixes before turning survivors into reviewable GitHub changes.
manifest.configuration_1: The gateway host needs git and an authenticated gh CLI; connect a GitHub repository, choose its base branch, and calibrate a ruler before performance runs.

manifest.description: A design critique you can run before you ask a colleague. Give it one screenshot, a whole multi-screen flow, a Figma file, a git repo, or a URL that is already serving, and it finds the candidate screens, lets you choose what to look at, then reports back the way an experienced designer would: an overall read, what is working, and the things worth tightening, each tied to a named heuristic. Multi-screen flows also get cross-screen findings that a single screen cannot show — inconsistent controls, missing progress, no way back, dead ends. It renders code and Figma before judging them, so it never critiques visuals it has not actually seen, and it says plainly which screens it could not get to instead of guessing.
manifest.highlight_1: Takes screenshots, a Figma link, a git repo, a local folder, or a running URL — and says back what it found before it starts
manifest.highlight_2: Measures contrast and hit-target sizes from the rendered page rather than estimating them from an image
manifest.highlight_3: Multi-screen flows get cross-screen checks: control consistency, progress, a way back, repeated asks, dead ends
manifest.highlight_4: Every finding names the heuristic behind it (Nielsen 1-10, WCAG, Gestalt, Fitts) and carries a severity on the NN/g 1-4 scale
manifest.highlight_5: Select any line of the report and ask a follow-up question about it, in place
manifest.highlight_6: Tells you what it could not see instead of critiquing a blank or blocked screen
manifest.highlight_7: Hands off the work it reviews: it never installs that project's dependencies, runs its scripts, starts its dev server, or edits its files
manifest.highlight_8: To take pictures it uses a headless browser, downloaded once into a cache in your home directory on first use and never into the project
manifest.use_case_1: Critique one screen or a complete product flow with severity-ranked, heuristic-backed findings tied to visible regions.
manifest.configuration_1: Drop in screenshots for zero-setup review, or provide a Figma file, repository, local folder, or already-running URL; private GitHub sources may require gh auth login.

manifest.description: An autonomous ops first responder. Watches your alarms, pages, and monitors; claims what fires; investigates it with real context; and proposes a fix — keeping everything it learns in a local ledger so the second occurrence is faster than the first.
manifest.highlight_1: Claims a firing alarm within one heartbeat and investigates before anyone has to look
manifest.highlight_2: Knowledge ledger with confidence and trust levels — a repeat failure resolves from what you already know
manifest.highlight_3: Live board in the dashboard and as replyable Slack threads, so the channel is the dashboard
manifest.highlight_4: Connects AWS CloudWatch, PagerDuty, Datadog, GitHub Issues, or any system that can POST signed JSON — including Alertmanager-shaped bodies, fanned out one incident per alert
manifest.highlight_5: Read-only by default — write actions are opt-in per signal pattern, and every one is audited
manifest.highlight_6: Rotation-aware: the on-shift automation tier arms and disarms itself
manifest.use_case_1: Watch operational signals, investigate incidents, reuse proven fixes, and hand over a complete local audit trail.
manifest.configuration_1: Add providers in Settings using environment credentials or provider tokens, keep Observe for read-only use, and explicitly opt into allowed Propose or Act actions; Slack output reuses an existing Kiro Crew connection.

manifest.description: A LaTeX paper editor with live PDF preview and an AI co-author. Write in a split-pane editor, press Cmd+S (Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) to compile with pdflatex or tectonic, and read the rendered PDF beside your source. Compilation errors are parsed into a clickable list that jumps to the offending line. Clone an existing paper from any git remote, then commit and push from the toolbar. The co-author panel is a real Kiro Crew chat session scoped to the paper, so the agent can read and edit your LaTeX while you watch the PDF update.

tailnetMobile.occupied_body: Tailscale is already serving something at this address, and publishing would replace it. Nothing was changed. Publish it yourself if you are sure it is safe to overwrite.
tailnetMobile.publish_title: Put the dashboard on your private network
tailnetMobile.publish_body: Everything is ready. This publishes the dashboard to your own Tailscale network only — never to the public internet — so your phone can open it.
tailnetMobile.ready_body: Open this address on a phone signed in to the same Tailscale network. Show a QR code to skip typing it.
tailnetMobile.qr_alt: QR code linking to this dashboard

tailnetMobile.keep_awake_note: This computer will not sleep while phone access is on, so the dashboard stays reachable. Its screen can still turn off.
tailnetMobile.no_peers: No other device has joined this Tailscale network yet, so nothing can open this address. Install Tailscale on your phone and sign in with the same account.
tailnetMobile.peers_offline: Your other devices have joined this network but none is online right now, so the address will not load until one connects.

webhooksPage.a_webhook_lets_an_outside_system_ci_a_re:
A webhook lets an outside system (CI, a review bot, a deploy pipeline) start
        one agent turn on this machine by POSTing a message with a bearer token.
webhooksPage.bearer_token_proves_who_is_calling: Bearer token — proves who is calling
webhooksPage.calls_must_send_signature_headers_detail: Calls with this token must send X-KiroCrew-Timestamp and X-KiroCrew-Signature. The signature covers "<timestamp>.<raw body>", the timestamp must be within ±{{seconds}}s, and each signature is accepted once per gateway process.
webhooksPage.calls_using_it_start_failing_with_401: Calls using it start failing with 401.
webhooksPage.completed_blurb: The agent turn finished and its answer was handed to the delivery targets.
webhooksPage.context_goes_stale_after_1_hour_and_expi:
Context goes stale after 1 hour and
        expires after 24 hours.
webhooksPage.copy_both_secrets_now_they_are_shown_onc: Copy both secrets now — they are shown once
webhooksPage.copy_this_token_now_it_is_shown_once: Copy this token now — it is shown once
webhooksPage.credential_not_recoverable_bearer: Your full secret was shown once at generation time and is stored only as a hash, so it cannot be looked up here or anywhere else. If you did not save it, revoke this token and generate a replacement, then update the system that calls it. Revoking is also the only way to invalidate a token that has leaked.
webhooksPage.credentials_not_recoverable_signed: Both the bearer token and the signing secret were shown once at generation time, and neither can be looked up here. If you did not save them, revoke this token and generate a replacement, then update the system that calls it. Revoking is also the only way to invalidate a token that has leaked.
webhooksPage.deleting_removes_the_stored_context: Deleting removes the stored context from {{file}}. That hook keeps working; its next call simply starts cold.
webhooksPage.disabled_blurb: Inbound webhooks were switched off, so the call was refused without checking its token.
webhooksPage.endpoint_url_unavailable_the_gateway_did: Endpoint URL unavailable — the gateway did not report one
webhooksPage.error_blurb: The agent turn failed before completing; the error was delivered instead of a result.
webhooksPage.expired_effect: The context is dropped. A call starts the agent cold with only the inbound message.
webhooksPage.fresh_effect: The next call to this hook receives the stored context injected verbatim.
webhooksPage.let_an_outside_system_wake_up_your_agent: Let an outside system wake up your agent
webhooksPage.no_call_has_arrived_for_this_hook_yet: No call has arrived for this hook yet.
webhooksPage.no_calls_recorded_yet_every_accepted_rej: No calls recorded yet. Every accepted, rejected, and unauthorized call lands here.
webhooksPage.no_summary_stored_for_this_hook: No summary stored for this hook.
webhooksPage.no_tokens_yet_until_one_exists_every_inb: No tokens yet. Until one exists, every inbound call is answered with 401.
webhooksPage.nothing_registered_an_agent_calls_the_re: Nothing registered. An agent calls the register_hook tool to leave context for a later inbound call.
webhooksPage.reference_below_still_describes_the_endp: Reference below still describes how the endpoint behaves.
webhooksPage.rejected_capacity_blurb: Every concurrent slot was busy, so the call was refused before a turn started. Retry with backoff.
webhooksPage.remove_setting_from_config_to_revoke: Remove {{setting}} from your config to revoke it.
webhooksPage.shown_in_the_bearer_only_form_because_no: Shown in the bearer-only form because no existing token requires a signature.
webhooksPage.shown_in_the_signing_form_because_the_to: Shown in the signing form because the tokens that can call this endpoint require a signature.
webhooksPage.shown_once_bearer_only_warning: This is the only time the full secret is displayed. {{productName}} stores just a hash of it, so it cannot be shown again or recovered. If you lose it, revoke the token and generate a new one.
webhooksPage.shown_once_signing_pair_warning: This is the only time these values are displayed. {{productName}} stores the bearer token only as a hash and never shows the signing secret again, so neither can be recovered. If you lose either one, revoke the token and generate a new one.
webhooksPage.signing_secret_proves_the_body_was_not_t: Signing secret — proves the body was not tampered with
webhooksPage.stale_effect: The context is still injected, but prefixed with an out-of-date warning so the agent verifies it before acting.
webhooksPage.started_the_agent_s_answer_arrives_in_no: started. The agent's answer arrives in notifications.
webhooksPage.that_action_did_not_go_through: That action did not go through
webhooksPage.this_token_is_accepted_on_the_bearer_hea: This token is accepted on the bearer header alone. A captured request can be replayed until the token is revoked.
webhooksPage.timed_out_blurb: The turn ran past its timeout and was cancelled. Partial work is not delivered.
webhooksPage.tokens_and_run_history_are_kept_you_can_: Tokens and run history are kept — you can switch it back on at any time.
webhooksPage.tool_the_agent_reads_it_before_the_inbou:
tool. The agent reads it
          before the inbound message so the turn resumes with the prior session's intent.
webhooksPage.unauthorized_blurb: The call did not authenticate: either the bearer token matched no active token, or its signature was missing, outside the timestamp window, replayed, or wrong. No turn was started and the caller is unknown.
